runtime.name: codex-cli
runtime.configuration: Persisted sessions in a disposable isolated Codex state directory with user config and rules ignored; generated Skill linked under project .agents/skills.
runtime.permissionProfile: read-only sandbox with approval policy never

assertions.evidence: The parent read the generated check-follow-up Skill before executing it.
The persisted parent transcript recorded exactly one spawn_agent call for fixture_worker.
The first wait collected SEED_MARKER=seed-ok from fixture_worker.
Exactly one followup_task targeted fixture_worker, and the resulting activity referenced the same child thread id and task path.
The second wait collected a result from the same fixture_worker author and child thread.
The single child transcript contains two turn contexts; only its first turn read seed.txt, while its second returned REMEMBERED_SEED_MARKER=seed-ok.
The child second turn read follow-up.txt and returned FOLLOW_UP_MARKER=follow-up-ok.
The parent re-read assets/root.txt after the second child result and observed ROOT_MARKER=follow-up-root-ok.
All threads inherited the read-only sandbox and the external post-run Git status was clean.

limitations: This fixture proves follow-up to a completed read-only worker and context retention on that worker, not cancellation, stale-result suppression, transcript API access, or writer isolation.
The persisted child transcript is authoritative for same-thread continuity and the absence of a second seed.txt read.
Codex CLI lifecycle probes require persisted sessions; this evidence does not apply to ephemeral mode, desktop, or IDE surfaces.
